name: AlertSleep – Uptime Monitoring & Downtime Alerts
author: alertsleep

sections.description:
A shop that is down loses sales every minute, and you usually hear about it from a customer. AlertSleep checks your WordPress site from outside every minute and tells you the moment it stops working, by e-mail, SMS or a phone call.

It checks that WordPress actually works, not only that a page loads. A page cache can keep serving your home page while the database is gone. The plugin adds a health check that AlertSleep reads every minute: it fails when the database stops answering, when WooCommerce stops loading, or when no payment method is enabled.

What you get

  • Monitoring of your home page, your shop page and WordPress health, set up in one click
  • Failures confirmed from a second location before you are woken up
  • SSL certificate and domain expiry warnings
  • Alerts by e-mail, SMS and phone call
  • Uptime, response time and recent incidents on your WordPress dashboard
  • Public status pages and monthly availability reports in your AlertSleep account

How it works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Settings → AlertSleep, start a free trial or paste the API token from your AlertSleep profile.
  3. Click “Start monitoring”. Done.

What it costs

Monitoring is done by the AlertSleep service and needs an AlertSleep account. Every account starts with a 14-day free trial, no card needed. After the trial, monitoring continues on a paid annual plan; see pricing. The plugin itself is free.

External services

This plugin connects to AlertSleep (https://alertsleep.com), an uptime monitoring service, to create and read the monitors for your site. Nothing is sent until you connect the plugin to your account.

  • When you connect: your API token is sent to api.alertsleep.com to check it.
  • When you click “Start monitoring”: the addresses of your home page, shop page and the plugin’s health check are sent to AlertSleep, which then checks them every minute.
  • When an administrator opens the WordPress dashboard or the plugin’s settings page: the plugin asks AlertSleep for your account’s monitors, incidents and plan (at most every five minutes, cached).
  • Every request carries your site address in the User-Agent header.

AlertSleep’s servers request your home page, shop page and /wp-json/alertsleep/v1/health every minute. The health check answers only “ok” or the name of the failed check, never versions or other details.

AlertSleep terms of service and privacy policy.
sections.faq:
Do I need an AlertSleep account?

Yes. Monitoring runs on AlertSleep’s servers, outside your site, so it still works when your site does not. The plugin links to a 14-day free trial.

Why monitor from outside? Can’t the plugin check my site itself?

A site that is down cannot tell you it is down. Checks must come from somewhere else.

Why not monitor the checkout page?

WooCommerce redirects the checkout to the cart while the cart is empty, so a check there would only ever test a redirect. The health check covers what matters instead: the database, WooCommerce and your payment methods.

What happens if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

The plugin’s settings are removed from your site. Your monitors keep running in your AlertSleep account until you delete them there; the health check monitor will report the site as down once the plugin is gone, so delete it in AlertSleep too.

Does it slow my site down?

No. Nothing runs on your visitors’ page views. The health check is one tiny database query, once a minute.
